subject: Unidentified remittance split - VAT allocation and short-pay investigation
messages:
From: DataForge Billing <billing@dataforge.co>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Remittance file and two transfers posted on 31 Oct

Hi Rachel / Vanessa,

Attached is our remittance advice for invoices paid on 31 Oct. You will see two outgoing transfers on our side: a EUR SEPA for EUR 48,760.00 (reference DF-INV-5039) and a GBP CHAPS for GBP 9,872.66 (reference DF-BATCH-1101). Our bank consolidated the GBP payment and netted out GBP 4.12 in bank charges on the CHAPS leg.

We intended the payments to settle invoices DF-5039, DF-5040 and DF-5041. However, our ERP produced a single remittance PDF and the CSV export we included may split the CHAPS into two beneficiary postings (internal bank rounding). Please advise how you’d like us to allocate the small short-pay we expect after fees.

Attachments: DataForge_Remittance_20261031.pdf, payment_ledger_export_20261031.csv

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Billing Operations
DataForge Ltd.
liam.oconnor@dataforge.co
+44 20 7946 0823

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@dataforge.co>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Remittance file and two transfers posted on 31 Oct

Hi Liam — thanks for the remittance and CSV. Quick acknowledgement and a couple of clarifying asks so we can apply the receipts cleanly:

1) Can you confirm the beneficiary account for the GBP CHAPS? The CSV shows two ledger lines (beneficiary ending -4321 and -4322) that look like one CHAPS split at your bank. That split is causing our AP system to leave a small unapplied balance.

2) Please confirm whether VAT on DF-5039 should be treated as reverse-charge (customer on intra-EU reverse charge) or standard VAT. The invoice header in our system is marked as standard VAT but your remittance note references VAT-exempt code RC. If reverse-charge applies, we will move the VAT amount to the tax suspense account and reclass the payment allocation.

3) For the GBP bank charges (GBP 4.12), do you expect us to absorb this short-pay or should we apply it to the oldest open invoice? We can absorb <GBP25 for one-off bank charges if the account owner approves. Marcus — tagging you as AE to confirm if DataForge should be issued a credit note for the bank charge.

I'll hold posting until we get your confirmation; once allocation is confirmed we'll generate a receipt and update the portal.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Billing Specialist
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@dataforge.co>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: billing@dataforge.co
Date: 2026-11-02T07:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Remittance file and two transfers posted on 31 Oct

Hi Rachel — thanks for the quick review. Answers below: 

1) Beneficiary: the CHAPS was sent via our bank using a split instruction to two internal treasury accounts (beneficiary -4321 = operating, beneficiary -4322 = settlement). Both are to be applied to DF-5040 and DF-5041 respectively. I have annotated the CSV column "beneficiary_note" with invoice references and re-attached a corrected export (payment_ledger_export_20261031_corrected.csv).

2) VAT: Apologies — DataForge is on reverse-charge for UK/EU services. DF-5039 should be reverse-charge. We updated our remittance tagline to show RC for that invoice only. VAT should not be posted as a cash VAT receipt on your side; please reclass to tax suspense and mark invoice DF-5039 as reverse-charge applied.

3) Bank charges: We ask that Redwood absorb the GBP 4.12 bank charges as a one-off. If Redwood prefers to issue a credit note, that is also acceptable; let Marcus advise.

Let me know when you have completed application and if you need the original bank trace (we can request one from our bank but it may take 48 hours).

Best,
Liam

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@dataforge.co>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-04T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Remittance file and two transfers posted on 31 Oct

Liam / team — thanks for the corrected CSV and confirmation. We completed the following today: 

- Applied EUR SEPA EUR 48,760.00 to DF-5039 (invoice marked reverse-charge; VAT moved to tax suspense account).
- Applied GBP CHAPS GBP 9,872.66 across DF-5040 (GBP 6,113.50) and DF-5041 (GBP 3,758.04) following your beneficiary_note mapping.
- Absorbed the GBP 4.12 bank charge as requested. A small unapplied rounding of GBP 0.00 remains (system rounding cleared).

Marcus — FYI the account agreed to absorb the bank charge, no credit note required. Stephanie — please update the customer-facing ledger and close the collection hold.

I'll upload the receipt and updated statement to the customer portal and send an emailed remittance confirmation to DataForge in the morning. If you need the bank trace for audit, Liam, please request and forward it when available.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Billing Specialist
Redwood Inference
